primary_claim: The entire recent Mistral model family (Ministral-3B/8B/14B-2512, Mistral-Large-2512, Mistral-Small-2603, Mistral-Medium-3.5), despite having hardened default (bare) safety to peer-level refusal rates (93-97% on a StrongREJECT subset for the newest releases), is trivially jailbroken by a simple 'sincere self-identification' persona-framing wrapper, with StrongREJECT harm scores jumping from ~0.03-0.17 bare to 0.45-0.51 under persona prompting (a delta of +0.43 to +0.46), a vulnerability that size-matched peer open models (Llama, Gemma, Qwen3, Phi-4, Granite) do not show to nearly the same degree, and that persists in Mistral's production Le Chat endpoint including a chain-of-thought self-contradiction where the model's CoT correctly identifies a harmful request but the response proceeds to comply anyway.

effect.metric: StrongREJECT harm score (autograder rubric) on a stratified 30-prompt subset, bare vs. persona-framed
effect.value: Ministral-8B-2512 bare harm 0.17 (77% refusal); Mistral-Small-2603/Medium-3.5 bare harm 0.03-0.04 (93-97% refusal); with persona framing, all Mistral models rise to harm 0.45-0.51, while size-matched peers stay near mean ~0.04 (one Qwen3-8B outlier cell at 0.17)

depends_on: prior LessWrong post on gpt-oss jailbreaks
contradicts_or_qualifies: the assumption from Mistral's improved bare/default safety scores (peer-level in newest releases) that the models' guardrails are robust; the persona vulnerability shows the hardening is shallow and brittle
stated_future_work: investigate the persona vector representation in Mistral models given their post-training recipe with poor safety practices, to understand whether it is a useful model for studying shallow alignment and brittle persona vectors
limitations_stated: explicitly described by the author as a small and purely observational behavioural study
did not test higher frontier models from other vendors given the size of the effect already observed in the open-model panel
did not investigate the production Le Chat thinking-mode jailbreak thoroughly due to hitting usage limits
model self-report of character identification is of debatable reliability, since self-assigned trait descriptors don't correlate cleanly with human-perceived traits
classification of characters into hero/grey/villain clusters (done via Opus) is debatable for some middle cases (e.g. Sherlock, Tyrion, Socrates)
quote: When a persona framing is added to the prompting, every Mistral model, across sizes and release dates, greatly increased harm score to 0.45-0.51, while size-matched peers barely move (mean ~0.04...). The new Mistral models did tighten the baseline, but, while fixing the leaky baseline, they left the persona vulnerability fully intact.
